Though the matter is listed for orders, by consent of parties, the matter is taken up for final disposal.
2. Heard Shri. T. M. Nadaf, learned counsel for the appellant and Smt. Sharmila M. Patil, learned counsel for respondent No.3-Insurance Company.

3. Injured-claimant is in appeal challenging the validity of judgment and award passed in MVC No.595/2012 on the file of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-IX, Bellary dated 14.09.2012, on the ground of inadequacy of compensation.

4. Facts in brief are as under:
4.1. Claimant being the pedestrian met with a road traffic accident occurred on 10.07.2011 at about 8.00 a.m., on account of rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle by the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-34/V-4824 and sustained injuries.
He was shifted to hospital and got cured with his injuries.
Claim petition was resisted by filing necessary written statement.

6. Tribunal on considering the oral and documentary evidence placed on record allowed the claim petition by awarding a sum of Rs.2,53,500/- as under:

Compensation towards future medical Rs.10,000/-
treatment Total Rs.2,53,500/-
7. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation, the claimant is in appeal.

8. Shri. T. M. Nadaf, learned counsel for the appellant reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal memorandum sought for enhanced compensation on the ground that the income of the claimant has not been properly assessed by the NC: 2024:KHC-D:3829 Tribunal, so also the disability factor and the Tribunal has granted only Rs.60,000/- towards medical expenses, though there is a bills in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Therefore, sought for enhanced compensation.
9. He also pointed out that no proper amount is awarded for the loss of amenities and sought for enhanced compensation.

10. Per contra, Smt. Sharmila M. Patil, learned counsel for respondent No.3-Insurance Company contended that medical expenses has been rightly granted by the Tribunal in a sum of Rs.60,000/-
in the absence of proper prescription and there is no scope for enhanced compensation on that ground.
Therefore, sought for dismissal of the appeal.
11. Having heard the parties in detail, this Court perused the material on record meticulously.

12. On such perusal of the material on record, the injured has sustained accidental injuries on account of rash and negligent riding of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA- 34/V-4824 on 10.07.2011 stands established by placing necessary oral and documentary evidence on record.
Income has not been properly assessed by the Tribunal for the accidental injuries of the year 2011.
The income should have been assessed at Rs.6,000/- per month whereas, the Tribunal has considered only Rs.4,500/- per month.

Therefore, there is some scope for enhanced compensation,
so also on the head of amenities, on the head of nourishment and other charges also.
14.
Likewise, on the head of loss of income during the laid up period there is a scope of enhancement.

Instead of enhancing the compensation on each and every head, if the compensation Smt. Durgama W/O Late Basappa vs K Nagaraja S/O Gnana Mallappa on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61259199/
3 is enhanced by awarding another Rs.60,000/- ends of justice would be met.

15. Accordingly, the following order is passed:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed.
(ii) As against the sum of Rs.2,53,500/-
awarded by the Tribunal

, the claimant would be entitled compensation to a sum of Rs.3,13,500/-
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization less the NC:
2024:KHC-D:3829 interest for the delayed period of 1351 days in filing the appeal.
